subject: Request: APAC bounded-failover window and DPA addendum
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@acme-fin.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@acme-fin.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: APAC pinning: bounded failover window & DPA addendum request

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up with our InfoSec and Procurement teams this morning and they raised two items that I wanted to put in writing:

1) APAC region pining — Acme needs a firm commitment that customer data for production workloads can be pinned to APAC (Singapore region) by default. We understand transient exceptions for DR, but InfoSec wants the transient window bounded (they suggested a maximum of 48 hours) and fully audited. Please confirm whether Redwood can commit to a bounded failover window and whether that window is configurable per-account.

2) DPA addendum & subprocessors — Procurement wants a DPA addendum that includes: list of APAC-region subprocessors, a short description of any transient cross-border egress during failover, and an explicit clause about proof-of-pin during the POC (we will ask for a signed attestation after onboarding).

Can you share a draft addendum and any one-pager that explains the operational controls for the APAC pin (how KV/cache replication is handled, whether cached tokens or logs will transit out of APAC, etc.)?

We'd like to get answers and a draft DPA before our procurement sync next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Sara Bloom
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme FinTech

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a short one-pager that outlines the APAC pin behavior and controls.
- Jonas will send a draft DPA addendum with the subprocessor roster and the legal language for transient egress.
- Vivek — can you confirm operational details around KV cache replication and whether temporary syncs to other regions are chunked/encrypted and observable in logs?

Sara — I'll follow up with a Doc link to the draft addendum and one-pager this afternoon. If you want to hop on a quick 30-min call for procurement and InfoSec alignment we can do Tuesday morning; otherwise we'll exchange drafts.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: APAC pinning questions from Acme

Kim / Vivek / Jonas — forwarding Acme's asks. A couple of technical notes from my side before we reply externally:

- KV cache & prefix caching: for APAC-pinned accounts we keep primary caches in the pinned region; we only replicate keys to other regions for warm failover. The replication is incremental and only transfers necessary KV fragments, not full model weights.
- Transient egress window: default is 48 hours but can be lowered to 4 hours for high-security customers; max can be extended by exception but will require justification + SOC evidence.
- Logs/audit: every transient egress event generates a structured audit entry (who/why/sequence) and a pre-signed snapshot we can provide on request during POC.

Vivek — can you confirm encryption-at-rest and in-transit for these KV sync paths (I believe TLS + per-tenant envelope keys via KMS)? Also please flag any subprocessor names that need to go into the DPA addendum.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Deployments
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@acme-fin.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: DPA addendum (draft) and subprocessor roster for APAC pinning

Sara — please find a short DPA addendum draft attached (link below). Key points called out:

- Residency commitment: Redwood will treat the customer account as APAC-primary for production workloads. Data at rest and primary inference request handling will remain in the pinned region except for temporary failover as described below.
- Bounded failover window: default 48 hours from incident/maintenance start; configurable to 4/12/24 hours on request. Any extension beyond default requires mutual written agreement.
- Transient egress definition: any requests or short-term replication that leave the pinned region for failover or diagnostic purposes. Transient egress is limited to metadata, KV fragments, and encrypted request envelopes — not model weights or backups.
- Audit & proof-of-pin: Redwood will provide structured audit logs for any transient egress and a signed attestation post-POC showing that production traffic remained APAC-primary outside of documented failovers.
- Subprocessors: included roster (third-party CDN for telemetry, KMS provider, cloud infra provider region nodes) — see appendix.

Attachments/links: DPA-addendum-draft.docx
Draft link: https://docs.redwood.example/dpa-addendum/Acme-POC

We're open to minor legal redlines but will need to review any material changes with Security/Product to ensure technical feasibility. If Acme needs shorter default windows (e.g., 4 hours) we'll require a short onboarding checklist and an SLA amendment.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.example
